full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the mortgagee-petitioner is directed against the judgment and decree dated 28.12.83 passed by Mr. Mustafizur Rehman, Upazilla Revenue Officer, Ramu as an authorised officer under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by President's Orders 88 and 136 of 1972 in Restoration Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1983-84. 

 4. Mr. M. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appeared for the petitioner and Mr. A. K M. Shafiqur Rahman appeared for the mortgagor opposite parties. During the hearing of the rule the question of maintainability of this revision under section 115 C.P.C. was raised by the opposite parties in this Rule. Mr. M. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate for the petitioner thereafter submits that it is a dispute relating to immoveable property and the Circle Officer (Revenue) decided the matter in public in presence of the parties and after taking evidence, therefore the proceeding before the Circle Officer, (Revenue) is a Civil proceeding and the Circle Officer (Revenue) acted as a Civil Court. In support of his contention the learned Advocate relied upon a decision of High Court Division, Comilla Bench reported in 35 DLR 209 wherein it was held that the proceeding before the S.D.O in that case under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was a civil proceeding pending in a Court. In that case the question for decision was whether in the suit before the Civil Court the period consumed before the Sub-divisional Officer in the proceeding under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is to be deducted under Section 14 of the Limitation Act in counting the period of limitation for the purpose of the suit instituted thereafter. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of that case the argument of Mr. M. Fazlul Karim does not help him in any way. The learned advocate further submits that Article 109 of the suspended Constitution the High Court Division had superintendence and control over all Court subordinate to it. In Proclamation Order No. 1 of 1982 it has also been provided in sub-section (1) of section 4 of the said proclamation that the High Court Division of the Supreme Court have such jurisdiction as is or may be conferred on it by law and sub-section (4) of the said provides that the law shall be binding on the High Court Division and the law declared by either Division shall be binding on all courts, other than Martial Law Tribunal or Courts or Administrative Tribunals. Relying upon the provision of Article 109 of the suspended Constitution read with sub-section 4 of section 4 the learned Advocate tries to impress that the Circle Officer (Revenue) as an authorised Officer under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is Subordinate to the High Court Division. 

 5. Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the mortgagor opposite parties submits that by P. O. 88 and 136 of 1972 section 95 of the State" Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been amended and it is placed in part I of the said Act and section 147 of the said Act provides for an appeal and the relevant provision runs as follows:— 

 Referring to the above provisions the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that the impugned order has been passed by the authorised officer who is a Revenue Officer under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. As such the remedy against the said order has been provided in sections 147 and 149 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 6. The learned advocate submits that sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Proclamation No. 1 of 1982 it has been provided for that the High Court Division of the Supreme Court shall have such jurisdiction as is or may be conferred on it by law. There is nothing in section 115 C.P.C. that any new power has been conferred upon the High Court Division to deal with anything beyond the scope of section 115 C.P.C. The learned Advocate submits that the exercise of the jurisdiction by the Revenue Officer as authorised Officer under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the proceeding before him may be of civil nature and the Civil Procedure Code has provided the procedure for deciding any civil dispute before any authority either it is Civil Court or tribunal. That by itself does not give the character that the authorised officer exercising power under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is subordinate to the High Court Division under section 115 C.P.C. Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman has referred to the provision of section 115 C.P.C. which runs as follows:- 

 7. The Bengal and Assam Civil Court Act has given the ties of Civil Courts and 'District Judge' has also been defined in the General Clauses Act and also in the Civil Procedure Code. The words 'Civil Court' has not been defined anywhere. Although a Court or an authority may have exercised 'a Civil Jurisdiction that by itself cannot be said to  be a civil Court. Even if it is a civil Court that does not indicate that it is subordinate to the High Court Division unless it is expressly or impliedly provided for.
